author: Edge
text:
Ifmyante wrote: The BSZ lesson isn't complete.

I'm trying to work out a way to get the reader to get the first bit of the lesson, then work try to work out the rest of it before being shown how I see it. Needs some thought.....

Anyway, I'd like you to consider the lesson, and, from chart research, work out how the BSZ can be traded. From where to where? TT or PAC? Allow for runners? Stops and other management.

It's all there on the charts, and soon enough I'll find an home for the lesson

IF, Am I correct in seeing the BSZ as a area for the ITs to get their liquidity. Its the FL where we are looking to trade. not the BSZ itself. Its just another trap. the BSZ itself is a indication the ITs are tricking and creating liquidity for themselves before price turns at our appropriate DP within the FL. We have to ask ourselves if we dont have a opportunity for ITs to get their liquidity on the approach, the turn in price is not as evident to us. So on the approach we want to see either:

- a BSZ -Compression - A swing hi low (to fake out)

Happy to be corrected

author: Ifmyante
text:
Edge wrote: IF, Am I correct in seeing the BSZ as a area for the ITs to get their liquidity.

Absolutely!

Its the FL where we are looking to trade. not the BSZ itself. Its just another trap.

Yup. It's very often used to get the retailers trading in the right direction, then take their stops. They love to get sellers in who'll soon buy from them at an higher price, and buyers to sell at lower.

the BSZ itself is a indication the ITs are tricking and creating liquidity for themselves before price turns at our appropriate DP within the FL. We have to ask ourselves if we dont have a opportunity for ITs to get their liquidity on the approach, the turn in price is not as evident to us. So on the approach we want to see either:

- a BSZ -Compression - A swing hi low (to fake out)

Happy to be corrected

Yes.

But

As much as the ITs love to use what the retailers think they know against them, they also have to show sometimes that the retailers' conceptions are right.

I say this so you can decide upon your definite first target.

The common "breakout and retrace" has to occur often enough for retailers to still use it::

Remember: A lot of what we do is technical, but most of it is the application of an understanding of what the retailers think they know about the market.

So, from the image above, where is the massive probability trade from and to?

Once we've established that, we can go on to discuss its fine tuning and management.
